description: This case study is the American Public Power Association's 2025 report on grid hardening practices at coastal public power electric utilities, supported by the U.S. Department of Energy. It is based on interviews with utility personnel and on regulator and utility best practices, and presents five utility case studies, the acknowledgements naming the U.S. Virgin Islands Water and Power Authority, Lewes Board of Public Works in Delaware, Guam Power Authority, the City of New Bern in North Carolina and Keys Energy Services in Florida. The executive summary groups the techniques into reinforcing infrastructure, through weather-resistant materials, pole replacement with metal, concrete or composite poles rated for winds up to 145 mph, undergrounding, elevated substations and transformers and redundancy through secondary lines, distributed energy and microgrids, and upgrading technologies such as smart grids and SCADA. It also covers the rationale for funding, mitigation approaches, community engagement and partners. Coverage is coastal and island utilities in the United States and territories. Access: PDF, free. Caveats: interview-based, with varying levels of implementation across utilities. It suits resilience investment and hardening planning studies, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
